rationale_overall: This week's pool is thin on genuine buildup catalysts and heavy on noise: youth/school robotics competitions (Brownsville, Memorial, Huntsville, Tewksbury), private-company items with no US ticker (SpaceX Starship static fire, Blue Origin New Glenn test flight, Skild AI/Zebra deal, humanoid robot marathon in Beijing), geopolitical/military reporting with no direct investable line (Iran uranium claims, Indian Army Pinaka rockets, South Korean satellite platform, Navy Coyote launcher), and keyword false-matches (RailTel 'rocket' surge is an Indian rail stock, not spaceflight). The Amazon-Globalstar deal is a real catalyst but Globalstar (GSAT) is a small illiquid satellite name outside our current buckets and would require displacing a core holding for a speculative bolt-on — not a clear enough edge over GOOGL, NVDA, RKLB, or SMR to force a swap. Nano Nuclear Energy's Argentina proposal and TSMC's AI-demand earnings reinforce theses already held via SMR and NVDA/GOOGL rather than surfacing a new name. Nothing here clears the bar of a clearly stronger rising-wave vehicle versus a current holding, so no changes this week.
